summary: Bubble and placeholder contracts pass their artifact tests. Phase 2 Forge intake is not connected to rendering and does not build the ForgeArt shape.
blocking_findings: F1 [Blocker] review-c: Phase 2 manifest intake is unreachable and does not produce the existing ForgeArt contract. `render.mjs` calls only `prepare(rel)` (line 44), and `prepare()` reads only the existing media `forge/manifest.json` (prepare.mjs lines 443-454); the CLI also calls only `prepare()` (line 483). `prepareWithManifest()` has no caller (lines 307-331), and its `spec.forge` has `framesByGesture` and absolute handoff paths instead of the `ForgeArt` fields `gestures`, `idle`, `gestureBox`, `scenes`, and public-relative paths (src/types.ts lines 22-40; scripts/forge.mjs lines 22-70). Therefore Phase 2 renders will not consume MANIFEST.tsv and cannot render its cut-outs through the current compositor contract. The T2.4 test checks only a few adapter values and does not prove the required output shape or Lily, Ben, and family fallbacks.
evidence: HEAD is 6ea086808ca6b95e06f3111935277c9d41e9a642; `git diff --quiet 6ea08680 HEAD` returned success, so audited HEAD is current.
The exact phase diff changes prepare.mjs, compositor components, layout/timeline, tests, and the track plan/strategy; it does not change content/storytime packages or render.mjs.
scripts/prepare.mjs:307-331 defines `prepareWithManifest`; lines 432-467 define the separate ordinary `prepare()` path; lines 469-483 expose only the ordinary path through the CLI.
scripts/render.mjs:14,44 imports and calls `prepare(rel)`; src/types.ts:22-40 and scripts/forge.mjs:22-70 define the ForgeArt fields and the legacy adapter.
scripts/render.mjs retains the established outputs `song.mp4`, `song-poster.jpg`, `song-phone.mp4`, and `song-phone-poster.jpg`; these filenames agree with spec.md:20 and test-strategy.md:109.
Spec.md:20 records `song.video`, `song.videoPhone`, `song.poster`, and `song.posterPhone`; the phase diff does not alter these package keys or package files.

The test strategy says Review C applies to CLI flags, defaults, exit codes, output paths, and pure contracts, with no route or page (test-strategy.md:166). UX browser review does not apply; frame sheets and the Daniel/Storytime look check provide visual acceptance (line 168).
The initial Thai filter scanned 2,144 files under content/storytime and emitted `residual_files=0`; it reported source residual characters but did not emit source text.
The handoff manifest tests report 108 rows, 25 each for Pat, Sam, Mia, and May, four each for w04 and w07, and four matching scene-file comparisons.
